newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end weaker, situationals lead market.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end weaker, situationals lead market.

text.p: Taiping Consolidated and Malpac Holdings shares surged to 12-month highs in heavy volume to buck the weak trend of the broader market.
The key Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks fell 8.56 points or 0.78 percent to 1,088.98. The Second Board index of small-cap issues was down 1.89 points to 574.03.

Dealers said property stock Taiping was driven by rumours of it selling a key property asset. Malpac rose on news that United Merchant Group was buying a 33 percent stake in the company, a stockbroking and financial services firm.
Dealers said there was speculation that Taiping may be looking to sell its entire interest in Sentul Raya, a mixed property development in Kuala Lumpur.
Taiping jumped 88 cents or 40.37 percent, to a year-high of 3.06 on the market's heaviest volume of 32.3 million shares.
"We heard about them selling their flagship project. But it could also just be rotational play," said an analyst at a Malaysian brokerage.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
